narrative.summaryIntro:
Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Trivandrum, Kerala, is one of the most important temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is the presiding deity of the royal Travancore state. The temple is known for its significance in Vaishnavite tradition and its unique architectural blend of Dravidian and Kerala styles. The main sanctum features an impressive gopuram and ornate pillared corridors characteristic of Kerala temple architecture.

The temple gained international attention in 2011 when its underground vaults were opened, revealing treasures of immense historical and monetary value. The temple remains an important pilgrimage site for devotees of Vishnu and attracts thousands of visitors annually. The temple's architectural beauty, combined with its spiritual significance and rich heritage, makes it a major tourist and pilgrimage destination in Kerala. The temple complex exemplifies the artistic and religious traditions of South India.
